title: LOTUS: learning-based online thermal and latency variation management for two-stage detectors on edge devices
problem: Two-stage object detectors on edge devices suffer from severe thermal issues and significant inference latency variations due to high computational demands and dynamic proposal counts across frames, requiring frequent runtime frequency adjustments.
motivation: Latency variations harm user experience and waste hardware resources on resource-constrained edge devices.
method: Proposes Lotus, a framework that dynamically scales CPU and GPU frequencies jointly using deep reinforcement learning in an online manner. The DRL agent learns to manage thermal and latency variations by making frequency decisions based on current system state. Implemented and evaluated on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and Mi 11 Lite mobile platforms.
key_novelty: Joint online CPU-GPU frequency scaling using deep reinforcement learning specifically tailored to manage thermal throttling and latency variations in two-stage object detectors on edge devices.
contributions: Lotus framework for online thermal and latency variation management in two-stage detectors on edge devices
Joint CPU-GPU dynamic frequency scaling using deep reinforcement learning
Demonstration of reduced latency variation and faster inference while maintaining lower temperatures
Implementation and evaluation on multiple edge platforms including NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and Mi 11 Lite
limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract provided.
primary_theme: Online thermal and latency management for edge object detection
